content_html:
If you've heard of the famous 7 Color Mountain, it's time to discover its lesser-known but equally impressive neighbor: the Red Valley. This destination, still off the radar of many tourists, offers surreal landscapes, with hills and mountains dyed in intense red tones, a product of the high concentration of iron oxides in the soil.

Where is it located?

The Red Valley is located in the region of Cusco, in the province of Canchis, more than 5,000 meters above sea level. It is located a few kilometers from Vinicunca, so many people visit it after having explored the Mountain of 7 Colors.

Route and access

There are two main ways to get to the Red Valley:

  1. From Vinicunca: After reaching the Mountain of 7 Colors, you can continue walking towards the Red Valley, which takes approximately 30 to 40 minutes additional.
  2. direct route: Some travel agencies offer tours that go directly to the Red Valley without passing through Vinicunca. This option is less common but ideal if you want to avoid the large influx of tourists on the other route.

What makes the Red Valley special?

  • Unique landscape: Unlike Vinicunca, the Red Valley extends into vast reddish hills, interspersed with green valleys and streams.
  • Fewer tourists: Despite being so close to Vinicunca, the Red Valley receives many fewer visitors, allowing for a calmer and more authentic experience.
  • Panoramic view: From its highest points, you can see the Andes in all their splendor, with snow-capped peaks and an immensity of natural colors.

Recommendations for your visit

Prior acclimatization: Due to the altitude, it is advisable to spend at least 1 or 2 days in Cusco before venturing out.
Appropriate clothing: Bring warm clothing in layers as the weather can change quickly.
Hydration and snacks: It is important to stay hydrated and bring energy snacks for the walk.
Sun protection: Despite the cold, solar radiation is intense, so wear sunscreen and sunglasses.

Is the Red Valley worth visiting?

Definitely yes. If you are already planning to visit Vinicunca, it is worth spending a little more effort to reach this natural wonder. The reward will be a landscape that seems taken from another planet and a much calmer experience than in the popular Montaña de 7 Colores.

If you are looking for a less conventional but equally impressive destination, the Red Valley is a mandatory stop on your adventure through Cusco.
